note: A first riff from two notes: the step says what is on the neck, which two notes are in play and what a riff is in doing words (a short phrase played again and again). The second section opens every note and changes one thing at a time. It moves to other keys and tempos.

exercise.title: A riff of your own
exercise.why: A riff is a short phrase played again and again, so two notes and one rhythm are enough to make one.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track. Under it is the neck with the notes of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale. Only {{1}} and {{5}} are in play, the two notes of a power chord, and the other dots are faded.
Make up a short riff from {{1}} and {{5}}: play them one after the other or both together, in a rhythm you can repeat. Then play the same riff again and again.
Keep going until you can repeat it without thinking about the next note.

Press Play below to start the backing track again. Every dot is in play now, with the {{1}} notes ringed.
Keep your riff and change one thing each time round: the rhythm, the order of the notes, or one note swapped for the dot next to it.
If the riff falls apart, go back to {{1}} and {{5}} alone for a few rounds.
